h2: Ultrasonic testing training for Chicago technicians, and where UT is used around the city
html:
Ultrasonic testing training for Chicago technicians, and where UT is used around the city

If you searched for ultrasonic testing training and arrived here, this page covers UT inspection work in Chicago; the courses sit on separate pages. Atlantis teaches ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I and Level II ultrasonic testing as self-paced online theory followed by a practical examination, and the Chicago training page explains how local employers run it. Below is where Chicago-area UT technicians actually work.

Start with the ultrasonic testing training course for method content, or with NDT Level 1 training if you are new to the field and want to see what Level I involves before you commit to a method. Chicago employers training a group should read NDT training in Chicago. Scanning practice is available on the Practical NDT ultrasonic simulator, and technicians aiming for the top rung can prepare through ASNT NDT Level III training. Certification itself is issued by your employer under its written practice, not by whoever ran the course.

Refining southwest of the city. ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery in Channahon Township has a capacity of 270,000 barrels a day across 12 major process units, and CITGO's Lemont refinery in Romeoville processes 183,000 barrels a day. Most UT hours there go on thickness readings at condition monitoring locations on piping and vessels, with shear-wave and phased array examination of repair welds during turnarounds. Illinois lets qualified owner-users set pressure vessel inspection intervals from API 510 or the NBIC, so readings have to be repeatable at the same locations from one campaign to the next.

Steel along the lake. Just over the Indiana line, Cleveland-Cliffs runs the Indiana Harbor works in East Chicago, and Gary Works, owned by Nippon Steel since its purchase of U.S. Steel, is due to start relining Blast Furnace No. 14 in 2026. Reline and outage work on integrated mills typically calls for weld examination and wall-thickness surveys on furnace shells, gas mains and cooling circuits, which is steady work for UT Level II technicians who can handle hot, dirty access.

Nuclear generation. Constellation operates all six Illinois nuclear stations, 11 reactors in total. Braidwood and Byron, the two pressurized water reactor sites, are receiving new main turbines in stages during refuelling outages, with the full uprate expected by 2029. In-service UT on reactor systems runs under ASME Section XI with personnel qualified to the licensee's own programme, so it is a specialist path rather than an entry-level one. The Illinois Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act gives the Illinois Emergency Management Agency, not the State Fire Marshal, jurisdiction over boilers and pressure vessels at nuclear facilities.

Two jurisdictional points shape any UT job in the metro:

  • The Illinois Act exempts cities of more than 500,000 people, and the City of Chicago Department of Buildings runs its own Boiler Inspection Bureau, listed by the National Board as a separate member jurisdiction.
  • Elsewhere in Illinois, the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety sets the cycle: power boilers every year, heating boilers every two years, pressure vessels every three.

For inspection rather than training, Chicago scopes are delivered under Atlantis NDT inspection services with crews mobilised from Houston, and pressure vessel inspection in Chicago covers the NDE that supports an owner's API 510 programme. To set up UT Level I or Level II training for a Chicago crew, send a Chicago training enquiry.
